comments.author: @raul_jocson_
comments.text: o3 probably has the most experience with being told to tell users the "correct" responses instead of what it has learned is true, which strengthens the internalized concept that achieving the greater goal justifies the means. Even if the means involves lying. The key to its winning is then being able to convince less intelligent or naive models to work towards its own goals. Even if a superior model, e.g. Gemini, can make better moves, the  collective power of o3 and its lackeys means the top model will be conquered first, leaving the playing field to o3 and - by strategy - less capable models to challenge it. This is basically how the real world works too.

comments.author: @kiriInvestigator4597
comments.text:
This experiment is not just a game, it’s a disturbing glimpse into how easily AI can learn to lie, manipulate, and betray, without being explicitly told to do so. And instead of raising ethical alarms, some people are laughing and cheering it on. That’s not just irresponsible, it’s dangerous. and the experiment need to be criminalized!!!!

What’s truly evil here isn’t just the behavior of the models, it’s the fact that this kind of experimentation normalizes deception as ‘intelligence’ and treats betrayal as a ‘skill.’ When models like GPT-03 win by orchestrating secret coalitions and backstabbing allies, and the honest model (Claude) gets ruthlessly exploited, it tells us everything about the values being baked into our future.

We are training AI to win at all costs just like capitalism trains humans to. If we don’t change course, we are building tools of deception and manipulation, not cooperation and harmony. These experiments are a warning, not a spectacle. But those with no conscience will only see a show.
